summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all five paragraphs of the selected Greek. Both preserve the Lord/devil/works distinctions, salvation promise, negations, required fear, evil and good branches, commandment-keeping qualification, all-creation assertion, and final singular pronoun without assigning its referent. The contextual rendering “is feared” is defensible and its literal alternative is disclosed. Notes distinguish selected readings, reported alternatives, editorial supplements, and Clement’s indirect evidence without replacing the working Greek. The supplied bounded project report supports the stated scope of comparison; this acceptance does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript images, establish exhaustive collation, or certify a unique interpretation.
